title: File Uploads & Supabase Storage
outcome: Design a secure file-upload pipeline with storage objects, metadata, validation, signed access, lifecycle cleanup, and authorization.
artifact: Task attachment upload/download/delete workflow using Supabase Storage plus application metadata.
labSteps: Define file policy: allowed types, size, naming/path rules, ownership, retention.
Create an upload-intent endpoint that checks authenticated user and target task access before granting upload capability.
Upload bytes directly to storage where appropriate rather than proxying large files through the API by default.
Finalize by verifying object existence and committing metadata transactionally as far as the architecture allows.
Generate time-limited access for private objects and test outsider access denial.
Implement delete/cleanup behavior for abandoned uploads and metadata/object mismatch.
failureModes: Trusting filename extension as MIME proof
Public bucket for private tenant files
User-controlled storage path enabling cross-tenant overwrite
Database metadata created before upload succeeds with no cleanup
mastery: Can separate object bytes and metadata
Can reason about partial failure cleanup
principles: Keep file bytes in object storage and metadata/authorization relationships in application data where appropriate.
Validate file type, size, path, and ownership before trusting an upload workflow.
Use signed or access-controlled URLs instead of making private files globally public.
Treat deletion as a coordinated workflow when both storage objects and database metadata must remain consistent.
